أساسيات تحليل البيانات باستخدام Excel5 أيام (25 ساعة)د. سارة العتيبييغطي البرنامج مهارات تنظيم البيانات وتنظيفها، واستخدام الدوال الشائعة والجداول المحورية، وبناء لوحات معلومات بسيطة لدعم القرار. يتضمن تمارين عملية على ملفات واقعية ومشروعاً ختامياً يعرض فيه المشاركون أبرز المؤشرات التي استخلصوها.1.850 ر.س
إدارة المشاريع وفق منهجية PMP8 أسابيع (بواقع لقاء أسبوعي)م. خالد الحربييتناول دورة حياة المشروع ومجالات الأداء ومهارات إدارة أصحاب المصلحة والمخاطر والجودة، مع تدريبات محاكية لأسئلة الاختبار. يخرج المشارك بخطة مشروع متكاملة قابلة للتطبيق في بيئة العمل.3.200 ر.س
الكتابة الإدارية والتقارير المهنية3 أيامأ. نورة القحطانييركز على صياغة المراسلات والتقارير الإدارية بوضوح واختصار، وتنظيم المعلومات في مقدمة وعرض وخلاصة تنفيذية. تشمل التدريبات إعادة كتابة نصوص مهنية وتقديم تغذية راجعة فردية.900 ر.س
الأمن السيبراني للموظفينيومانم. عبدالله الشمريبرنامج توعوي عملي حول كلمات المرور والتصيد الاحتيالي وحماية الأجهزة والبيانات، مع سيناريوهات محاكاة للهجمات الشائعة. يهدف إلى تعزيز السلوك الآمن وتقليل المخاطر اليومية في بيئة العمل.600 ر.س
تصميم عروض تقديمية مؤثرة4 أيامأ. ريم الدوسرييجمع بين مبادئ التصميم البصري وبناء قصة العرض واختيار الوسائط المناسبة، ويطبق المشاركون خطوات إعداد عرض من الفكرة إلى العرض النهائي. تُقيَّم العروض وفق وضوح الرسالة وتناسق التصميم وجودة الإلقاء.1.100 ر.س
المحاسبة المالية لغير المحاسبين6 أيامد. محمد الأنصارييشرح المفاهيم المحاسبية الأساسية والقوائم المالية وتحليل النسب دون افتراض خلفية محاسبية سابقة. يستخدم أمثلة مبسطة من قطاعات مختلفة لتمكين المشاركين من قراءة الأرقام وتفسيرها في سياق القرار الإداري.2.000 ر.س
table.brief: دورات تدريبية: اسم الدورة / المدة / المدرب / الوصف (طويل) / الرسوم

understanding.purpose: A catalog of accredited training courses that readers scan to compare offerings and shortlist by course topic, duration, trainer, and fee; the description supports the choice after the course name is identified.
understanding.reading: Right-to-left: the eye starts at the rightmost course-name column as the row anchor, then moves left through duration and trainer metadata, the descriptive text, and finally the fee at the far left; cross-row comparison is strongest on course name, duration, trainer, and fee.
groups: col 1 (اسم الدورة) is the row anchor and identity column
col 2 (المدة) and col 3 (المدرب) are delivery metadata and scan together
col 4 (الوصف) is narrative detail, read after the shortlist
col 5 (الرسوم) is a separate commercial figure and should remain compact and intact
keep_intact: course-name words, especially the 67px longest token
duration numbers and their unit words
header labels, especially المدرب and الرسوم
may_wrap: course names at word boundaries when necessary
duration phrases such as "5 أيام (25 ساعة)" at spaces
trainer names into two lines if needed

preferred.name: r3A
preferred.note: Refines r2B: give the name column the 10px it was missing (170→180) so its longest titles break into two balanced lines instead of an orphaned tail, and add 2px to the description (290→292) to protect the 5-line row rhythm. The 14px comes out of duration and trainer, which are already multi-line without setting any row height (row 2 duration = 4 short lines ≈108px, still under the 129px row the description dictates).

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Prioritize table compactness: widen the description to 290 to reduce its line count and row heights, while keeping the fee at 91 for one-line amounts. Course name, duration and trainer tighten but remain above their longest unbreakable words and wrap only at spaces.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Pushes the elastic column to 300px (279px text) to test whether the narrative can drop from 5 lines to 4 in the shorter rows, while keeping every column above its unbreakable-word floor (name 67, duration 50, trainer 55, description 73). Name is trimmed to 172px — still two clean lines — betting that a shorter, denser table beats a slightly larger anchor.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: The opposite trade: restore the anchor to r2A's 190px so the course name reads solidly, funded entirely from the description (292→280) and small trims to duration/trainer, whose wrapping costs no height. Keeps 91px on the fee because 70px of text plus padding is the exact one-line minimum; tests whether anchor strength justifies one extra line of narrative per row.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Start from r1A and fix the fee first: widen the fee column 69→91 so '1.850 ر.س' stays on one line. Take the 22px from duration (−8), trainer (−11), and description (−3), keeping the course-name anchor at 190. Since row height is set by the description, these small reductions should not add rows, while the fee becomes scannable.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Alternative tradeoff: restore a stronger course-name anchor at 205px and keep the fee one-line at 91, accepting a narrower description at 258. This tests whether easier row identification outweighs taller description rows.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Refines r0B: keep the description at 275px (254px text) so the longest prose still lands at about six lines, but move 15px from the description and 5px from the trainer to widen the name from 170 to 190px. Duration stays at 90px, and trainer remains 95px (74px text), enough to keep honorifics with the first name. All longest words still fit without mid-word splits.

bad.name: r1B
bad.note: Refines r0A: preserve its 210px course-name anchor, but cut duration from 110 to 88 and trainer from 110 to 95, giving 37px to the description (220 to 257). Description text rises from 199 to 236px, reducing the eight-line prose ribbon. Trainer stays safe for two-line names, duration still fits its longest word, and the fee remains compact.
bad.why: The description is squeezed to 257px while the course-name column is given 210px, producing the tallest table (952px) and a cramped reading column; the 69px fee column also splits the amount from the currency, so a semantic unit breaks across lines.

rationale: In this RTL course catalogue the eye enters at the course name on the right, then reads the description, with duration, trainer and fee as supporting facts. r3A gives the description the dominant share (292px) while keeping the course-name row header wide enough to avoid most unnecessary label breaks, and it keeps the fee column at 91px so “1.850 ر.س” stays on one line. The narrower duration and trainer columns wrap their short contents, but row height is driven by the description, so those wraps cost no vertical space; the result is the shortest table (813px) with no mid-word splits and no wrapped headers.

general: Allocate width by reading and comparison role, not by symmetry: narrative or descriptive columns usually deserve the largest share, while short numeric or currency columns need just enough width to keep units intact.
The row-header column must stay scannable but should not rival the main body column; if it becomes too wide, it steals lines from the content that sets row height.
Widen the column that determines row height until it reduces line count; adding width to short secondary columns often adds no compactness.
Keep semantic units such as amount plus currency together even when no word is split mid-character.
specific: This is an Arabic RTL course table: the course name is the rightmost row header, the description is the body, and duration/trainer/fee are secondary attributes.
At 15px, the fee column needs about 91px to keep “ر.س” beside the amount; 69px forces a two-line fee cell.
A description width around 292px lets the third row drop to fewer lines, which is why r3A reaches 813px while similar designs with 280–290px descriptions grow taller.
Duration and trainer can be as narrow as 76–78px here because their cells are shorter than the description and therefore do not determine row height.

tradeoffs: The main disagreement is how much width the course-name row header deserves versus the description. A designer prioritizing maximum description measure might choose the 172/300 split of r3B; I chose 180/292 because it keeps more course labels intact without increasing table height. Another tradeoff is accepting wrapped duration/trainer cells in exchange for a wider description, which works here because those cells are not the tallest.
uncertain: Whether a two-line fee cell is a genuine publication fault or merely a minor compromise; whether r3A and r3B are effectively equal given browser text rounding; and the exact description-width threshold where a line drops may shift slightly with font rendering.

critique.good: The course-name column stays at 210px, all five headers fit on one line, the fee remains intact, and duration/trainer are comfortable enough to avoid mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The table is very tall at 1069px. The description becomes a narrow 220px ribbon of eight-line prose, while duration and trainer each receive 110px, more than their short metadata needs. The eye crosses two wide metadata columns before reaching a cramped narrative column.
critique.cause: The 220px description column (199px text) forces the longest description into about eight lines. The 110px duration and trainer columns consume 220px that could relieve the description. Row height is set by the description, not by the metadata.

critique.good: This is the most compact and scannable design. The 290px description brings the longest prose to six lines and the table to 836px. Headers fit, the fee stays intact, and there are no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The 170px course-name column (149px text) is the row anchor but wraps every course name into two short lines, sometimes leaving a lone word, PMP, or Excel on the second line. The 90px duration column (69px text) forces the long 8 أسابيع phrase into three lines. The identity column feels subordinate to the description.
critique.cause: Giving 290px to the description left only 170px for the name and 90px for duration. The name’s 250px one-line width cannot fit, and the duration’s 168px phrase cannot fit, so both wrap. The 100px trainer column is more generous than necessary.

critique.good: Course names are essentially one line at 271px (250px text), creating a very strong right-hand row anchor. The fee stays compact and intact, and all headers fit.
critique.problems: The table is extremely tall at 1278px, with rows up to 246px. The description at 190px (169px text) becomes a ten-line narrow column, while the name gets 271px for content that needs 250px. The 94/95px metadata columns are also cramped, making row units hard to compare.
critique.cause: The 190px description is far too narrow for a 1420px one-line cell, so it dictates ten-line rows. The 271px name column takes 38% of the table width for one-line identities, leaving insufficient width for the narrative detail.

critique.good: The strongest of the two: the description has the widest column, so rows are shorter than in r1B; all five headers stay on one line; the course-name anchor is adequate; no mid-word splits occur.
critique.problems: The fee column is too narrow: '1.850 ر.س' breaks into the number and the currency on separate lines, making the commercial figure less scannable and the far-left column look cramped. The description still drives very tall rows at 7 lines, and the first duration wraps.
critique.cause: col5=69 leaves 48px of content, below the 70px needed for a one-line fee, so the currency wraps. col4=275 leaves 254px of content and still produces about 7 description lines, which sets most row heights. col2=90 leaves 69px, below the 168px one-line duration width, so '5 أيام (25 ساعة)' wraps.

critique.good: The wider course-name column at 210px gives the row anchor more room, and the headers still fit on one line with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The table is taller than r1A (952px vs 906px), and rows 3, 5 and 6 grow to 153px because the description is narrower. The 20px moved from description to course name did not prevent long course names from wrapping, so it bought little while making the narrative column more ragged. The fee still splits number and currency.
critique.cause: col4=257 leaves only 236px of content, forcing more description lines, and the description is the tallest cell in most rows. col1=210 is still below the 250px one-line course width, so long names wrap anyway. col5=69 remains below the 91px needed for a one-line fee.

critique.good: Header row stays on one line, no mid-word splits, fee reads cleanly as one intact figure, and every row is legible with a two-line course name at a comfortable 190px anchor.
critique.problems: Tallest table of the three (906px) and visibly uneven: row 2 balloons to 176px while the first body row is 129px. The longest course name strands 'PMP' alone on its second line, and the duration cell in row 2 shreds '8 أسابيع (بواقع لقاء أسبوعي)' into four short lines. Meanwhile the fee column carries ~21px of unused slack next to the cramped trainer and duration cells.
critique.cause: Description at 272px (251px text) sits just below the threshold where the long narratives collapse from 6–7 lines to 5; name at 190px (169px text) lands in the zone where the longest titles break with a one-word tail; fee at 91px is already the minimum for a one-line fee, so its extra room is unavoidable but wasted while duration (61px text) is too narrow to hold a phrase.

critique.good: Shortest and most rhythmic result: 836px total with five of six body rows at exactly 129px (5 lines), so the table reads as a calm grid. Description at 290px (269px text) is the sweet spot for this text volume; headers unwrapped, fee intact, no mid-word splits, no orphaned words in duration or trainer.
critique.problems: The course-name column is the narrowest of the three (170px) even though it is the row anchor: longest titles break into two lines with a short tail ('Excel', 'PMP', 'المحاسبين'), making the right edge of the table look ragged and weaker than the description block it introduces. Row 1 is still 153px while the rest are 129px.
critique.cause: Allocating 290px to the text-hungry description consumed the budget, leaving only 170px (149px text) for the identity column, which needs roughly 10–15px more to break its longest names into balanced halves rather than a stub.

critique.good: The identity column at 205px is the best of the three: course names break evenly, the header area feels generous, and the right edge of the table reads as a solid anchor.
critique.problems: Narrowest description (258px → 237px text) makes every row gain a line: total height 952px, tallest cell 7 lines, heights jump 176/153/129/153. Duration at 80px forces '5 أيام (25 ساعة)' onto three lines and row 2's duration onto four, and the table as a whole looks vertically stretched with a fat identity column and a thin narrative column.
critique.cause: The 35–47px added to the name column were taken from the description, which is the most line-elastic column (1420px of one-line text) — each 10px removed there costs roughly a line per row, so the anchor gain is paid for several times over in height.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

ref_equal.why: The description column is far too narrow, so every row becomes a tall block and the table is dominated by vertical scrolling, while course/duration/trainer get excessive width. The main reading column is sacrificed.

ref_auto.why: The description is generously wide and rows stay compact, but the course column is too narrow, breaking long titles into three lines, and the fee column splits amounts like '1.850 ر.س' into two lines, weakening row identity and price scanning.

r2B.why: Best balance: fees stay on one line, the description is the widest of the balanced layouts, and course/duration/trainer wrap only modestly. Rows remain compact and easy to follow, though the duration column is still tight.

r3A.why: Course and description are readable and fees are intact, but the duration column is too narrow: values such as '5 أيام (25 ساعة)' and '8 أسابيع (بواقع لقاء أسبوعي)' break into three or four lines, adding height and interrupting comparison.

r3B.why: Very close to D; the course column is comfortable and fees are intact, but duration remains severely cramped and the description is slightly narrower than C, so some rows grow unnecessarily tall.

r1B.why: The widest course column keeps row titles clearer, but it steals width from the description and especially duration; duration values fragment into many lines and the table becomes taller and less scannable than C.

raw.unsure: Exact pixel widths are hard to verify from the screenshots, and D/E are nearly identical; B's split currency may be tolerable in some house styles.

r3A.why: Balanced RTL layout: course titles and fees stay readable, but the description is slightly tight and the duration breaks into three short lines.

r1B.why: Description gets generous width, but the fee column is too narrow: currency symbols wrap onto separate lines from amounts, disrupting numeric scanning.

r3B.why: Best overall balance: description is wide enough for efficient reading, course titles wrap cleanly, fees stay on one line, and no column looks wasteful.

r2B.why: Clean and readable with intact fees; the trainer column is a little over-wide at the expense of the description, but rows still scan well.

ref_auto.why: Description remains usable, but the course-name column is too narrow, breaking titles into three lines and making the table unnecessarily tall.

ref_equal.why: Description is squeezed into a narrow vertical strip while the trainer column is over-wide and mostly empty, producing tall rows and destroying scan rhythm.

raw.unsure: Exact pixel widths are estimated visually; C and D are close, and the main judgement hinges on whether the duration column’s extra line breaks matter more than description width.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
